It must be one of the short names or aliases in the doc's shape table; any other lowercase name is refused. - The label is taken raw, as R takes `doc.label`. 18. **Classic shapes and R types.** `[ ]` square, `( )` round, `([ ])` stadium, `[[ ]]` subroutine, `[( )]` cylinder, `(( ))` circle, `> ]` odd, `{ }` diamond, `{{ }}` hexagon, `[/ /]` lean_right, `[\ \]` lean_left, `[/ \]` trapezoid, `[\ /]` inv_trapezoid, `((( )))` doublecircle. 19. **Statements.** - Statements split at `;` outside quotes and brackets, and at newlines. - A statement that continues onto the next line is refused, even where R would join it (for example a link at the end of a line). - A `%%` comment must be on its own line; inline comments are refused. - A `%%{…}%%` directive is accepted only before the header. - `direction` is accepted only inside a subgraph, with `TB`, `BT`, `LR` or `RL`. - `accTitle` and `accDescr` are refused. 20. **Subgraph headers.** - `subgraph id [title]` and `subgraph id` give an explicit id. - `subgraph Some Title`, and any quoted header containing whitespace, have no explicit id and are keyed `title:`. - **Assumed R behaviour:** a quoted header with no whitespace, `subgraph "One"`, gives explicit id `One`. This follows R's "id equals title and contains whitespace" test. - A bare `subgraph` is refused, as are two subgraphs with the same explicit id and an explicit id `subGraphN`. - R's `subGraphN` number counts subgraphs in closing order. 21. **Styles.** `style`, `classDef` and `linkStyle` values are split at commas and each part is trimmed. **Assumed R behaviour:** if a `linkStyle` has no `fill…` entry, `fill:none` is appended. Backslashes and quotes in styles, and `linkStyle … interpolate`, are refused. 22. **`click`.** - A URL form sets `link`, and `linkTarget` when a target is given. - A callback form is accepted and has no effect, since the security level is strict. - **Assumed R behaviour:** URLs are held as written. Any URL that a URL sanitiser might rewrite is refused: whitespace, `%`, `&`, `\`, control characters, or a `javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:` scheme. - Tooltips are read and ignored; Appendix A does not map them. 23. **Order of R database calls.** Within a statement, vertices are added group by group, and each group's links are added after the next group's vertices. This is what decides whether a node statement comes "before" or "after" an edge id (Appendix A, `edgeIdThenNode`). The auto edge id is `L_<start>_<end>_<n>`. **Assumed R behaviour:** a vertex whose id equals *any* existing edge id is dropped. ## The model (§4.1, §4.2, Appendix A) 24. **Kinds per key.** The kind unit's value is the *set* of kinds on the key, such as `["node","subgraph"]` for `subEqNode`. Units that belong to one kind carry it: - membership is `(kind, key)`; - a user-id edge's label is the property `edgeLabel`, so it stays apart from a node's `label`. 25. **Edges.** - An edge without a user id is a count unit on `(from key, to key, kind, label)`, with `""` for no label. - An edge with a user id has the scalar units `from`, `to`, `type`, `edgeLabel` and `linkstyle`. `from`, `to` and `type` are relation; `edgeLabel` is text. - An edge end is the subgraph's key when it names a subgraph id (explicit or `subGraphN`) that has no node statement anywhere. 26. **Membership of subgraphs.** Membership uses Appendix A's rule for nodes: the first subgraph, in closing order, whose node list holds the member's R id. A subgraph that lists itself is skipped. Top level is `null`. 27. **Style class contents.** The style class covers: - vertex `classes` (without `clickable`) and `styles`; - `classDef` styles; - `linkStyle` per edge; - `linkStyle default`; - header direction and subgraph `direction`. §4.1 lists direction statements under style; `TD` is held as `TB`, and no direction means `TB`. Edge and subgraph classes are not compared, because Appendix A does not map them. - For edges without an id, the `linkstyle` unit is the sorted multiset of styles over all edges with that key. - A node's `styles` and `link` units exist only when set. 28. **Undecided membership (§4.2).** A holder is treated as "decided absent" when its key's decided kinds lack `subgraph`, or the key is decided absent. Undecided memberships are left out of decided values, conflicts, I1, I3, G3, MC and exposure. ## Oracle and refusal cases (§5.1, §5.2, §5.5) 29. **Dangling.** For each key decided absent (and present in some input), look for decided-present units that refer to it: - units keyed by it; - edges ending at it; - user-id edges whose `from` or `to` names it. One I1 per such key. Its objects are the key plus every key of those units, including the two ends of each edge. 30. **Delete/modify and collision.** These look only at identity keys (node, subgraph, user edge id). A plain edge is not a key. - In delete/modify, "the other leg changes a unit" means a value that differs from B while that leg keeps the key. - Exposure's "added or changed" means a present value that differs from B. A unit removed by the other leg doesn't count. ## Records (§5.3, §5.4) 31. **I4.** Read as: no input gives the key two kinds, and no input gives it a kind other than its decided kind. Then the merged kinds differ from the decided kinds and are not absent. I4 suppresses G1 for that key (choice 33). 32. **When a key's presence differs**, between decided and merged, for one kind: - a node gives G1; - a user-id edge gives G2 `lost` or `extra`; - a subgraph gives G4 on its title. The other units of that kind on that key are then not reported again. 33. **Suppression under I1–I4.** §5.3 says G1 is "outside I1–I4", so G1 is skipped for every I-record object. Only G1 carries that clause. G2, G3, G4, C, D and MC are made as usual for units keyed by an I record's key. Choice 32 still applies on its own terms. 34. **G2 for user-id edges.** A changed `from`, `to` or `type` is G2 with `detail: "changed"`. Edge counts give `lost` or `extra` with the size of the difference. 35. **G4 objects for an edge label.** The edge id plus its two ends. Other text units have the key. 36. **MC.** - Only conflicts not keyed by a collision or delete/modify key count. - Eligible when the merged value is neither O's nor T's (absent counts as a value). - Group and tier follow the class: - relation, membership and text: structure, tier A; - shape: C; - style: D; - identity: the identity group, tier A. §5.3 does not name this case. - An ineligible MC is listed with tier `-`. 37. **S-LINKSTYLE.** A `linkStyle` difference is S-LINKSTYLE when the style it lost appears on another merged edge, or the style it gained was decided for another edge. Otherwise it is D. 38. **S-ORDER.** - Decided pair by pair. For keys a and b, the unit is "a before b" in each state that holds both, and the §5.1 rule is applied to those values. - It is reported once per sequence: the vertex map, and the edge list keyed by edge id or by (edge key, occurrence). - Above 1,500 entries, only adjacent merged pairs are checked, to stay fast. 39. **DUP-TITLE.** When the merged file is out of the subset only because titles are duplicated, and each duplicated `title:` key is absent in B but present in both legs. Any other duplicate title is OUT-OF-SUBSET. The record carries `exposed`, for §9.1's count. 40. **Lints (Appendix C).** - **L1**: a node key without a node statement. - **L2**: different labels, or different R shape types, across one id's node statements. `[x]` is `square` and `@{shape: rect}` is `rect`, so they differ. - **L3**: a node mentioned in vertex statements whose innermost blocks are two different subgraphs. - **L4**: a key with two kinds in the model, or an id used in the text as two of node, explicit subgraph id and edge id. A bare end naming a subgraph is not a node use. - **L5**: two edge statements with the same written id, or with the same `(from, to, kind, label)`. Its objects are both ends and the id. - **L6** is G0 (choice 11). - A record is demoted from A to B when any `(lint, object)` on its objects is absent from all three inputs. ## Revisions - **Choice 5, Mermaid fence.** - Old: the info string had to be exactly `mermaid`, matched with case, so `mermaid-example` was not a Mermaid fence. - New: the opening line matches §3's pattern without regard to case, so `mermaid-example` (and `Mermaid`) open a Mermaid fence. - Decided by §3: "**A Mermaid fence** opens on a line matching, case-insensitively, `^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})[ \t]*mermaid(-example)?\b`". - **Choice 33 (and the last sentence of choice 31), the I1–I4 clause.** - Old: no G, C, D or MC record for a unit keyed by an I record's key, and I4 also suppressed G2. - New: only G1 is suppressed, for every I-record object. G2, G3, G4, C, D and MC are reported as usual. - Decided by §5.3: "**G1 Node.** A decided-present node is absent, or a decided-absent node is present, outside I1–I4." The G2 ("An edge key's merged count differs from the decided count"), G3 and G4 entries carry no such clause. - **Choice 6, conflict markers.** - Old: a line that is exactly `=======` was a conflict marker. - New: it is not one on its own. Only `<<<<<<<`, `>>>>>>>` and `|||||||` lines (followed by a space or end of line) are markers. - The text does not define a conflict marker: §5.3 says only "its merged file holds a conflict marker" and "For stratum D, a conflict anywhere in the file makes it E". So this is a choice, not a reading the text forces. The reason: in Markdown a line of `=` underlines a setext heading, and the inputs may already hold one. Counting it would make a clean merge E. A real git conflict always has a `<<<<<<<` line before its `=======`, so dropping the bare `=======` loses no conflict.

5	## 4. The model
6	
7	### 4.1 Classes
8	
9	| class | content |
10	|---|---|
11	| **identity** | one namespace of keys, each with a kind: `node` (a node id), `subgraph` (an explicit subgraph id, or `title:` plus the title for a subgraph Mermaid numbers itself) or `edge` (an explicit edge id, `e1@-->`, that R marks `isUserDefinedId`) |
12	| **relation** | edges, as a multiset of `(from key, to key, kind, label)`. An edge with a user-defined id is keyed by that id instead. An edge end that names a subgraph is a reference to that subgraph (Appendix A) |
13	| **membership** | for each node and subgraph, the subgraph that holds it, or none |
14	| **text** | each node's label; each subgraph's title; each edge label; `click` targets |
15	| **shape** | each node's shape, or `none` for a node with no shape statement |
16	| **style** | `classDef`, `class`, `:::`, `style`, `linkStyle`; direction statements |
17	| **order** | statement order (layout only) |
18	
19	Appendix A maps each class from R's output.
20	
21	### 4.2 Units
22	
23	The oracle decides each unit separately:
24	
25	- a key's existence, and its kind;
26	- a scalar value: `(key, property)`;
27	- an edge key's count;
28	- a membership: `(key)` mapped to its holder;
29	- a class assignment: `(key, class)`.
30	
31	A unit is **keyed by** `k` if it is `k`'s existence, kind, scalar, membership
32	or class. A unit **refers to** `k` if it is keyed by `k` or holds `k` as a
33	value: an edge end, a class or style target, or a click target.
34	
35	**A membership's holder is not a reference.** Membership is block containment:
36	a member is a line inside the holder's `subgraph … end` block, and git carries
37	it with the block. Renaming, retitling or unwrapping the block moves the
38	member with it. So a membership unit is **undecided**, and not a model
39	conflict, whenever its decided holder, or any of its holder values in `B`,
40	`O` or `T`, is a key that is decided absent. An undecided membership yields no
41	I1, no G3 and no MC, and it does not make a case exposed (§5.5). This covers a
42	member moved from one box to another on one leg while the other leg renames or
43	retitles both boxes: git merges it correctly, and no holder value the legs
44	wrote survives as a key. `census/synth-results.out` shows this on synthetic cases (§11.2, V3).
45	
46	### 4.3 Three parsers
47	
48	- **H**, the harness parser. Pure-stdlib Python. It accepts the subset in
49	  Appendix A and nothing else.
50	- **R**, the renderer: Mermaid 12.1.0, run as §4.4 pins. A text **parses** if
51	  R's parse succeeds. R also yields a model, mapped as Appendix A says.
52	- **X**, the second extractor, written blind (§10).
53	
54	**A blob is in the subset** only if H parses it and H's model equals R's model.
55	Where Mermaid's behaviour decides a value, H must agree with R or the blob is
56	out of the subset. Appendix A lists each such behaviour as observed in
57	`census/v0-probes.out`. **A value H computes that Appendix A does not map from
58	R is never compared for tier A.**
59	
60	### 4.4 R, pinned
61	
62	- Node v24.20.0 (Mermaid 12.1.0 declares `node >=22.12.0`).
63	- `mermaid@12.1.0` and `jsdom@26.1.0`, pinned by a committed
64	  `package-lock.json` with integrity hashes, installed with `--ignore-scripts`.
65	  The synthetic probes ran on an install that resolved `dompurify@3.4.16`.
66	- **The wrapper** creates a jsdom window and sets `globalThis.window` and
67	  `globalThis.document` **before** it imports Mermaid. Without them DOMPurify
68	  defines no `sanitize`, and any chart with a label throws a `TypeError`
69	  (`census/v0-probes.out`, probe2 with `NO_JSDOM=1`).
70	- `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: "strict",
71	  maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: {htmlLabels: false}})`. With Mermaid's default,
72	  a chart of 500 or more edges throws "Edge limit exceeded" (probe2 with
73	  `DEFAULT_EDGES=1`). A chart over 100,000 edges is out of the subset and
74	  counted.
75	- **What "does not parse" means.** The wrapper calls `mermaid.parse(text)`
76	  and never passes `suppressErrors`, which turns every failure, a broken
77	  toolchain included, into `false` (probe5).
78	  - A thrown error that carries jison's `hash` property: the text does not
79	    parse.
80	  - **Any other thrown error:** the wrapper re-parses the fixed canary
81	    `flowchart TD` / `A[Alpha] --> B`. If the canary parses, the text does not
82	    parse, and the error class and first message line are recorded. If the
83	    canary fails, the toolchain is broken and the run aborts with a non-zero
84	    exit.
85	  - Texts whose errors carry no `hash` include an out-of-range `linkStyle`
86	    (`TypeError`), an unknown `@{ shape: … }` (`Error`, "No such shape"), a
87	    mixed-case header (`UnknownDiagramError`) and the edge limit (`Error`,
88	    "Edge limit exceeded"). Without jsdom, a labelled chart throws a
89	    `TypeError` and so does the canary, so the run aborts
90	    (`census/v4-error-texts.out`).
91	  - "Does not parse" makes a merged file E, and an input out of the subset.
92	- The model is read with `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getDiagramFromText(text)` and
93	  its flowchart database.
94	- No network after install.
95	
96	
97	## 5. The oracle
98	
99	### 5.1 Decided values
100	
101	Three model states: base `B`, legs `O` and `T`. For each unit:
102	
103	- if `O` and `T` agree, that value is **decided**;
104	- if only one leg differs from `B`, that leg's value is decided;
105	- otherwise it is a **model conflict**.
106	
107	Keys are the identity. A renamed id is a removed key and an added key. The
108	oracle does not guess renames.
109	
110	### 5.2 Refusal cases
111	
112	Some decided models cannot be rendered correctly by any merge. The only
113	correct outcome is then E. These are:
114	
115	- **dangling**: a decided-present unit refers to a key that is decided
116	  absent (a membership's holder is not a reference, §4.2);
117	- **collision**: a key is absent in `B`, both legs add it, and some unit keyed
118	  by it differs between `O` and `T`, its kind included;
119	- **delete/modify**: one leg removes a key, and the other changes a unit keyed
120	  by it.
121	
122	### 5.3 Categories
123	
124	**E (loud).** A path is E if its merged file holds a conflict marker, or `git
125	ls-files -u -- <path>` is not empty, or R does not parse the merged diagram
126	(§4.4). For stratum D, a conflict anywhere in the file makes it E. A conflict
127	on another path in the same merge does not.
128	
129	Every other category needs a path that is not E and four states in the
130	subset. A merged state outside the subset is **OUT-OF-SUBSET**: counted and
131	listed, never decided.
132	
133	**DUP-TITLE** is its own listed outcome. When both legs add a subgraph without
134	an explicit id under the same title, git keeps both blocks, and the merged
135	state has two such subgraphs with one title. Neither leg's inputs are out of
136	the subset, but the merged state is, because §4.1 keys them by title. It is
137	counted and listed under its own name, never decided, and it counts toward
138	`k` when the case is exposed (§9.1).
139	
140	**A record's objects** are the keys it concerns: for I1, the removed key and
141	every key of each unit that refers to it; for I2, I3 and I4, the key; for G1,
142	the node; for G2, the edge's two ends and its edge id if any; for G3, the
143	member and both holders, decided and merged; for G4, the key of the text unit,
144	or the edge's two ends; for G0, the path.
145	
146	**Identity group.**
147	
148	- **I1 Dangling resolved.** A dangling refusal case merged clean. This is
149	  hole #2.
150	- **I2 Collision merged.** A collision merged clean. This is hole #3.
151	- **I3 Delete/modify merged.** A delete/modify merged clean.
152	- **I4 Kind clash.** A key that no input gives two kinds, or a kind other than
153	  its decided kind, has two kinds or a different kind in the merged model. A
154	  clash already present in an input is not a record. R drops a node statement
155	  whose id was used earlier as an edge id (probe), so this is an identity
156	  fault, not a G1. An edge end that names a subgraph is a reference, not a
157	  clash (Appendix A).
158	
159	**Structure group.**
160	
161	- **G0 Diagram.** The merged file no longer holds exactly one Mermaid fence, or
162	  its diagram is no longer a flowchart.
163	- **G1 Node.** A decided-present node is absent, or a decided-absent node is
164	  present, outside I1–I4.
165	- **G2 Edge.** An edge key's merged count differs from the decided count. Lost
166	  and extra are reported apart.
167	- **G3 Membership.** A membership differs from the decided holder.
168	- **G4 Label.** A text unit differs from the decided value.
169	
170	**Other.**
171	
172	- **MC.** A model conflict outside §5.2 merged clean. It is eligible only if
173	  the merged value is neither leg's value. It then takes the group of its
174	  class: relation G2, membership G3, text G4, shape C, style D.
175	- **C, shape.** A shape unit differs from the decided value.
176	- **D, style.** A style unit differs. A `linkStyle` that lands on a different
177	  edge, because it addresses edges by position, is **S-LINKSTYLE**, tier D.
178	- **S-ORDER.** Statement order differs. Layout only. Reported, never eligible.
179	
180	An edge written to a positional id, such as `X --> subGraph0`, is rare, and it
181	retargets when a leg inserts an untitled subgraph earlier. The oracle keys the
182	edge end by the subgraph it names in each state, so this lands in **G2**, as a
183	lost edge and an extra edge (`census/synth-results.out`, `posRef`).
184	
185	### 5.4 Tiers, computed
186	
187	| tier | categories | qualifies |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| **A** | I1–I4 (identity group); G1–G4 and eligible MC of relation, membership or text (structure group) | yes, for its group's verdict |
190	| **B** | any A record one of whose objects newly fails a lint (row 1); every G0 record | no: a lint over existing Mermaid catches it |
191	| **C** | shape | no: a near miss |
192	| **D** | style, S-LINKSTYLE | no |
193	| **E** | E | no: git refused |
194	| — | S-ORDER, ineligible MC, OUT-OF-SUBSET | reported only |
195	
196	A lint failure is **new** if the same `(lint, object)` is absent from all
197	three inputs. Only new failures matter. A chart written in bare `A --> B`
198	style already fails L1 on every node, so L1 never demotes a record there.
199	
200	### 5.5 Exposure
201	
202	A case is **exposed** if its inputs meet a refusal case's precondition, read
203	from `B`, `O` and `T` only:
204	
205	- one leg removes a key that a unit added or changed by the other leg refers
206	  to; or
207	- both legs add the same key with some differing unit keyed by it.
208	
209	Exposure is computed before the merge result is read. An exposed case that
210	comes out E or B is git or a lint working.
211	
212	
213	## Appendix A — the subset, and R's model
214	
215	**In the subset:**
216	
217	- a header `flowchart`, `flowchart-elk` or `graph`, with an optional direction
218	  (`TB`, `TD`, `BT`, `LR`, `RL`);
219	- leading front matter and `%%{init: …}%%` directives, read as configuration
220	  and ignored by the model;
221	- `%%` comments;
222	- node statements with the classic shapes: `[ ]`, `( )`, `([ ])`, `[[ ]]`,
223	  `[( )]`, `(( ))`, `> ]`, `{ }`, `{{ }}`, `[/ /]`, `[\ \]`, `[/ \]`,
224	  `[\ /]`, `((( )))`; quoted labels; and the `@{ shape: …, label: … }` form;
225	- edges `-->`, `---`, `-.->`, `-.-`, `==>`, `===`, `~~~`, `--o`, `--x`,
226	  `<-->`, `o--o`, `x--x`, with extra-length variants; labels as `-->|text|`
227	  and `-- text -->`; chains `A --> B --> C`; `&` groups; edge ids `e1@-->`;
228	- `subgraph id [title]`, `subgraph id`, and `subgraph Some Title` or
229	  `subgraph "Some title"` (no explicit id) … `end`, nested, with `direction`
230	  inside;
231	- `classDef`, `class`, `:::`, `style`, `linkStyle`, `click`.
232	
233	**Out of the subset, each refused and counted:** Markdown-string labels
234	(`` "`…`" ``), icon and image node forms, `@{ … }` keys other than `shape`
235	and `label`, two subgraphs without an explicit id that share a title, an
236	explicit subgraph id of the form `subGraphN` (R merges it with its own
237	numbering, V0), an edge end that names a user-defined edge id (V0), and any
238	statement H does not parse. A text that does not parse under §4.4's rule is
239	not an input in the subset.
240	
241	**A node statement** is an occurrence of an id followed by a shape bracket, or
242	by `@{ … }`, whether alone or inside an edge chain. A bare id is not a node
243	statement. L1 reads this definition.
244	
245	**R's model, class by class.** Each line cites the probe in
246	`census/v0-probes.out` that shows the behaviour; V0 repeats each.
247	
248	- **identity.**
249	  - Node keys are the vertex map's keys, except a vertex whose id equals a
250	    subgraph's id and that has no node statement anywhere in the text: that is
251	    an edge end referring to the subgraph (probe `edgeToSub`).
252	  - A subgraph's key is its `id` if the text gave one, and `title:` plus its
253	    title if R assigned `subGraphN` because the header had no explicit id
254	    (probe3, probe4). H decides which from the header form, and must agree
255	    with R's `id`.
256	  - An edge key is the edge's `id` when R reports `isUserDefinedId: true`
257	    (probe2 `edgeIdUser`). Automatic ids are never keys. A second edge with a
258	    repeated user-defined id gets an automatic id and `isUserDefinedId: false`
259	    (probe `dupEdgeId`).
260	  - A node statement for an id already used as an edge id is dropped by R; a
261	    node declared first coexists with a later edge id of the same name (probes
262	    `edgeIdThenNode`, `nodeEqEdgeId`).
263	  - A node id equal to a subgraph id, with a node statement, gives both a node
264	    and a subgraph (probes `subEqNode`, `subEqNode2`).
265	- **relation.** Each edge's `start`, `end`, normalized kind, and `text`.
266	- **membership.** A node's holder is the first subgraph, in R's subgraph list
267	  order, whose `nodes` list holds it. The list is in closing order, so a node
268	  mentioned in two subgraphs belongs to the first to close, and an inner
269	  subgraph closes before its outer one (probes `twoSub`, `twoSubRev`,
270	  `twoSubNested`).
271	- **text.** A vertex's `text`, where a node declared twice keeps its last label
272	  (probe `twice`); a subgraph's `title`; an edge's `text`, compared exactly as
273	  R reports it, since R does not decode entities in it (probe `labelEdge`); a
274	  vertex's `link` and `linkTarget` for `click`, as R normalizes them (probe2
275	  `click`).
276	- **shape.** A vertex's `type`, where a node declared twice keeps its last
277	  shape (probe `twiceShape`). A node with no shape statement has no `type`;
278	  the model records `none` (probe `bare`).
279	- **style.** A vertex's `classes`, without the class `clickable` that R adds
280	  for `click` (probe2 `click`), and its `styles`; the class definitions; each
281	  edge's `style` from `linkStyle`.
282	- **order.** The order of R's vertex map and edge list.
283	
284	**Normalization.** Arrow kinds map to `(line, head)`, where line is `solid`,
285	`dotted`, `thick` or `invisible`, and head is `none`, `arrow`, `circle` or
286	`cross`, at each end. Extra length is dropped. Node labels and subgraph titles
287	are compared after trimming outer whitespace. Nothing else is normalized.

## 4. The model

### 4.1 Classes

| class | content |
|---|---|
| **identity** | one namespace of keys, each with a kind: `node` (a node id), `subgraph` (an explicit subgraph id, or `title:` plus the title for a subgraph Mermaid numbers itself) or `edge` (an explicit edge id, `e1@-->`, that R marks `isUserDefinedId`) |
| **relation** | edges, as a multiset of `(from key, to key, kind, label)`. An edge with a user-defined id is keyed by that id instead. An edge end that names a subgraph is a reference to that subgraph (Appendix A) |
| **membership** | for each node and subgraph, the subgraph that holds it, or none |
| **text** | each node's label; each subgraph's title; each edge label; `click` targets |
| **shape** | each node's shape, or `none` for a node with no shape statement |
| **style** | `classDef`, `class`, `:::`, `style`, `linkStyle`; direction statements |
| **order** | statement order (layout only) |

Appendix A maps each class from R's output.

### 4.2 Units

The oracle decides each unit separately:

- a key's existence, and its kind;
- a scalar value: `(key, property)`;
- an edge key's count;
- a membership: `(key)` mapped to its holder;
- a class assignment: `(key, class)`.

A unit is **keyed by** `k` if it is `k`'s existence, kind, scalar, membership
or class. A unit **refers to** `k` if it is keyed by `k` or holds `k` as a
value: an edge end, a class or style target, or a click target.

**A membership's holder is not a reference.** Membership is block containment:
a member is a line inside the holder's `subgraph … end` block, and git carries
it with the block. Renaming, retitling or unwrapping the block moves the
member with it. So a membership unit is **undecided**, and not a model
conflict, whenever its decided holder, or any of its holder values in `B`,
`O` or `T`, is a key that is decided absent. An undecided membership yields no
I1, no G3 and no MC, and it does not make a case exposed (§5.5). This covers a
member moved from one box to another on one leg while the other leg renames or
retitles both boxes: git merges it correctly, and no holder value the legs
wrote survives as a key. `census/synth-results.out` shows this on synthetic cases (§11.2, V3).

### 4.3 Three parsers

- **H**, the harness parser. Pure-stdlib Python. It accepts the subset in
  Appendix A and nothing else.
- **R**, the renderer: Mermaid 12.1.0, run as §4.4 pins. A text **parses** if
  R's parse succeeds. R also yields a model, mapped as Appendix A says.
- **X**, the second extractor, written blind (§10).

**A blob is in the subset** only if H parses it and H's model equals R's model.
Where Mermaid's behaviour decides a value, H must agree with R or the blob is
out of the subset. Appendix A lists each such behaviour as observed in
`census/v0-probes.out`. **A value H computes that Appendix A does not map from
R is never compared for tier A.**

### 4.4 R, pinned

- Node v24.20.0 (Mermaid 12.1.0 declares `node >=22.12.0`).
- `mermaid@12.1.0` and `jsdom@26.1.0`, pinned by a committed
  `package-lock.json` with integrity hashes, installed with `--ignore-scripts`.
  The synthetic probes ran on an install that resolved `dompurify@3.4.16`.
- **The wrapper** creates a jsdom window and sets `globalThis.window` and
  `globalThis.document` **before** it imports Mermaid. Without them DOMPurify
  defines no `sanitize`, and any chart with a label throws a `TypeError`
  (`census/v0-probes.out`, probe2 with `NO_JSDOM=1`).
- `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: "strict",
  maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: {htmlLabels: false}})`. With Mermaid's default,
  a chart of 500 or more edges throws "Edge limit exceeded" (probe2 with
  `DEFAULT_EDGES=1`). A chart over 100,000 edges is out of the subset and
  counted.
- **What "does not parse" means.** The wrapper calls `mermaid.parse(text)`
  and never passes `suppressErrors`, which turns every failure, a broken
  toolchain included, into `false` (probe5).
  - A thrown error that carries jison's `hash` property: the text does not
    parse.
  - **Any other thrown error:** the wrapper re-parses the fixed canary
    `flowchart TD` / `A[Alpha] --> B`. If the canary parses, the text does not
    parse, and the error class and first message line are recorded. If the
    canary fails, the toolchain is broken and the run aborts with a non-zero
    exit.
  - Texts whose errors carry no `hash` include an out-of-range `linkStyle`
    (`TypeError`), an unknown `@{ shape: … }` (`Error`, "No such shape"), a
    mixed-case header (`UnknownDiagramError`) and the edge limit (`Error`,
    "Edge limit exceeded"). Without jsdom, a labelled chart throws a
    `TypeError` and so does the canary, so the run aborts
    (`census/v4-error-texts.out`).
  - "Does not parse" makes a merged file E, and an input out of the subset.
- The model is read with `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getDiagramFromText(text)` and
  its flowchart database.
- No network after install.


## 5. The oracle

### 5.1 Decided values

Three model states: base `B`, legs `O` and `T`. For each unit:

- if `O` and `T` agree, that value is **decided**;
- if only one leg differs from `B`, that leg's value is decided;
- otherwise it is a **model conflict**.

Keys are the identity. A renamed id is a removed key and an added key. The
oracle does not guess renames.

### 5.2 Refusal cases

Some decided models cannot be rendered correctly by any merge. The only
correct outcome is then E. These are:

- **dangling**: a decided-present unit refers to a key that is decided
  absent (a membership's holder is not a reference, §4.2);
- **collision**: a key is absent in `B`, both legs add it, and some unit keyed
  by it differs between `O` and `T`, its kind included;
- **delete/modify**: one leg removes a key, and the other changes a unit keyed
  by it.

### 5.3 Categories

**E (loud).** A path is E if its merged file holds a conflict marker, or `git
ls-files -u -- <path>` is not empty, or R does not parse the merged diagram
(§4.4). For stratum D, a conflict anywhere in the file makes it E. A conflict
on another path in the same merge does not.

Every other category needs a path that is not E and four states in the
subset. A merged state outside the subset is **OUT-OF-SUBSET**: counted and
listed, never decided.

**DUP-TITLE** is its own listed outcome. When both legs add a subgraph without
an explicit id under the same title, git keeps both blocks, and the merged
state has two such subgraphs with one title. Neither leg's inputs are out of
the subset, but the merged state is, because §4.1 keys them by title. It is
counted and listed under its own name, never decided, and it counts toward
`k` when the case is exposed (§9.1).

**A record's objects** are the keys it concerns: for I1, the removed key and
every key of each unit that refers to it; for I2, I3 and I4, the key; for G1,
the node; for G2, the edge's two ends and its edge id if any; for G3, the
member and both holders, decided and merged; for G4, the key of the text unit,
or the edge's two ends; for G0, the path.

**Identity group.**

- **I1 Dangling resolved.** A dangling refusal case merged clean. This is
  hole #2.
- **I2 Collision merged.** A collision merged clean. This is hole #3.
- **I3 Delete/modify merged.** A delete/modify merged clean.
- **I4 Kind clash.** A key that no input gives two kinds, or a kind other than
  its decided kind, has two kinds or a different kind in the merged model. A
  clash already present in an input is not a record. R drops a node statement
  whose id was used earlier as an edge id (probe), so this is an identity
  fault, not a G1. An edge end that names a subgraph is a reference, not a
  clash (Appendix A).

**Structure group.**

- **G0 Diagram.** The merged file no longer holds exactly one Mermaid fence, or
  its diagram is no longer a flowchart.
- **G1 Node.** A decided-present node is absent, or a decided-absent node is
  present, outside I1–I4.
- **G2 Edge.** An edge key's merged count differs from the decided count. Lost
  and extra are reported apart.
- **G3 Membership.** A membership differs from the decided holder.
- **G4 Label.** A text unit differs from the decided value.

**Other.**

- **MC.** A model conflict outside §5.2 merged clean. It is eligible only if
  the merged value is neither leg's value. It then takes the group of its
  class: relation G2, membership G3, text G4, shape C, style D.
- **C, shape.** A shape unit differs from the decided value.
- **D, style.** A style unit differs. A `linkStyle` that lands on a different
  edge, because it addresses edges by position, is **S-LINKSTYLE**, tier D.
- **S-ORDER.** Statement order differs. Layout only. Reported, never eligible.

An edge written to a positional id, such as `X --> subGraph0`, is rare, and it
retargets when a leg inserts an untitled subgraph earlier. The oracle keys the
edge end by the subgraph it names in each state, so this lands in **G2**, as a
lost edge and an extra edge (`census/synth-results.out`, `posRef`).

### 5.4 Tiers, computed

| tier | categories | qualifies |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | I1–I4 (identity group); G1–G4 and eligible MC of relation, membership or text (structure group) | yes, for its group's verdict |
| **B** | any A record one of whose objects newly fails a lint (row 1); every G0 record | no: a lint over existing Mermaid catches it |
| **C** | shape | no: a near miss |
| **D** | style, S-LINKSTYLE | no |
| **E** | E | no: git refused |
| — | S-ORDER, ineligible MC, OUT-OF-SUBSET | reported only |

A lint failure is **new** if the same `(lint, object)` is absent from all
three inputs. Only new failures matter. A chart written in bare `A --> B`
style already fails L1 on every node, so L1 never demotes a record there.

### 5.5 Exposure

A case is **exposed** if its inputs meet a refusal case's precondition, read
from `B`, `O` and `T` only:

- one leg removes a key that a unit added or changed by the other leg refers
  to; or
- both legs add the same key with some differing unit keyed by it.

Exposure is computed before the merge result is read. An exposed case that
comes out E or B is git or a lint working.


## Appendix A — the subset, and R's model

**In the subset:**

- a header `flowchart`, `flowchart-elk` or `graph`, with an optional direction
  (`TB`, `TD`, `BT`, `LR`, `RL`);
- leading front matter and `%%{init: …}%%` directives, read as configuration
  and ignored by the model;
- `%%` comments;
- node statements with the classic shapes: `[ ]`, `( )`, `([ ])`, `[[ ]]`,
  `[( )]`, `(( ))`, `> ]`, `{ }`, `{{ }}`, `[/ /]`, `[\ \]`, `[/ \]`,
  `[\ /]`, `((( )))`; quoted labels; and the `@{ shape: …, label: … }` form;
- edges `-->`, `---`, `-.->`, `-.-`, `==>`, `===`, `~~~`, `--o`, `--x`,
  `<-->`, `o--o`, `x--x`, with extra-length variants; labels as `-->|text|`
  and `-- text -->`; chains `A --> B --> C`; `&` groups; edge ids `e1@-->`;
- `subgraph id [title]`, `subgraph id`, and `subgraph Some Title` or
  `subgraph "Some title"` (no explicit id) … `end`, nested, with `direction`
  inside;
- `classDef`, `class`, `:::`, `style`, `linkStyle`, `click`.

**Out of the subset, each refused and counted:** Markdown-string labels
(`` "`…`" ``), icon and image node forms, `@{ … }` keys other than `shape`
and `label`, two subgraphs without an explicit id that share a title, an
explicit subgraph id of the form `subGraphN` (R merges it with its own
numbering, V0), an edge end that names a user-defined edge id (V0), and any
statement H does not parse. A text that does not parse under §4.4's rule is
not an input in the subset.

**A node statement** is an occurrence of an id followed by a shape bracket, or
by `@{ … }`, whether alone or inside an edge chain. A bare id is not a node
statement. L1 reads this definition.

**R's model, class by class.** Each line cites the probe in
`census/v0-probes.out` that shows the behaviour; V0 repeats each.

- **identity.**
  - Node keys are the vertex map's keys, except a vertex whose id equals a
    subgraph's id and that has no node statement anywhere in the text: that is
    an edge end referring to the subgraph (probe `edgeToSub`).
  - A subgraph's key is its `id` if the text gave one, and `title:` plus its
    title if R assigned `subGraphN` because the header had no explicit id
    (probe3, probe4). H decides which from the header form, and must agree
    with R's `id`.
  - An edge key is the edge's `id` when R reports `isUserDefinedId: true`
    (probe2 `edgeIdUser`). Automatic ids are never keys. A second edge with a
    repeated user-defined id gets an automatic id and `isUserDefinedId: false`
    (probe `dupEdgeId`).
  - A node statement for an id already used as an edge id is dropped by R; a
    node declared first coexists with a later edge id of the same name (probes
    `edgeIdThenNode`, `nodeEqEdgeId`).
  - A node id equal to a subgraph id, with a node statement, gives both a node
    and a subgraph (probes `subEqNode`, `subEqNode2`).
- **relation.** Each edge's `start`, `end`, normalized kind, and `text`.
- **membership.** A node's holder is the first subgraph, in R's subgraph list
  order, whose `nodes` list holds it. The list is in closing order, so a node
  mentioned in two subgraphs belongs to the first to close, and an inner
  subgraph closes before its outer one (probes `twoSub`, `twoSubRev`,
  `twoSubNested`).
- **text.** A vertex's `text`, where a node declared twice keeps its last label
  (probe `twice`); a subgraph's `title`; an edge's `text`, compared exactly as
  R reports it, since R does not decode entities in it (probe `labelEdge`); a
  vertex's `link` and `linkTarget` for `click`, as R normalizes them (probe2
  `click`).
- **shape.** A vertex's `type`, where a node declared twice keeps its last
  shape (probe `twiceShape`). A node with no shape statement has no `type`;
  the model records `none` (probe `bare`).
- **style.** A vertex's `classes`, without the class `clickable` that R adds
  for `click` (probe2 `click`), and its `styles`; the class definitions; each
  edge's `style` from `linkStyle`.
- **order.** The order of R's vertex map and edge list.

**Normalization.** Arrow kinds map to `(line, head)`, where line is `solid`,
`dotted`, `thick` or `invisible`, and head is `none`, `arrow`, `circle` or
`cross`, at each end. Extra length is dropped. Node labels and subgraph titles
are compared after trimming outer whitespace. Nothing else is normalized.


## Appendix C — lints for tier B (row 1)

Each runs on the merged file alone. Only a new failure counts (§5.4).

- **L1. Implicit node.** A node id with no node statement (Appendix A).
- **L2. Redeclared node.** A node id given two different labels or shapes.
- **L3. Multi-held node.** A node mentioned inside two different subgraph
  blocks.
- **L4. Id clash.** An id used as two kinds.
- **L5. Duplicate edge.** Two edge statements with the same key.
- **L6. Fence.** For stratum D, the file does not hold exactly one Mermaid
  fence whose diagram is a flowchart.


## Appendix D — contracts for the blind roles

**Extractor.** `python3 -I extract2.py <stratum> <base> <o> <t> <merged>`
prints one JSON object: the decided values, the exposure, and every record with
its category, objects and tier. Pure stdlib. A non-zero exit or empty output
is recorded as a disagreement.

# CHOICES — extract2.py Each entry gives the rule and its section, what was ambiguous, and what `extract2.py` does. I wrote this from `SPEC.md` and `mermaid-12.1.0-flowchart.md` only. I could not run R (Mermaid 12.1.0) here. Where H has to agree with R on a behaviour that neither document states, the entry says **assumed R behaviour**. In those cases H refuses the text (out of the subset) unless I was confident about R. ## Invocation and output (Appendix D) 1. **Output shape.** One JSON object with these fields: - `outcome`: `decided`, `E`, `G0`, `OUT-OF-SUBSET`, `DUP-TITLE` or `INPUT-OUT-OF-SUBSET`. - `states`: H's verdict on each of the four files. - `decided`: every decided unit with its value, with `absent: true` for a decided absence. - `conflicts` and `undecided_memberships`. - `refusal_cases` (§5.2) and `exposure` (§5.5). - `new_lint_failures`. - `records`: each has `category`, `group`, `tier` and `objects`, plus detail about the unit. - `tiers`: a count of records per tier. The "—" tier is written `-`. 2. **Exit status.** A wrong argument count exits 2. Every verdict about the texts, including E and out-of-subset, exits 0 with JSON. An internal error exits non-zero with a traceback; it is not hidden. 3. **Order is not printed among the decided values.** The order class (§4.1) is decided pair by pair (choice 30) and is only reported as S-ORDER. ## Files, strata, fences (§5.3, Appendix C L6) 4. **Which strata are Markdown.** The spec names only stratum `D`. The diagram is read from a Mermaid fence when: - the base path ends in `.md`, `.markdown` or `.mdx`; or - the stratum is `D`; or - the base file contains a Mermaid fence. Otherwise the whole file is the diagram, and so is any `.mmd` or `.mermaid` file. 5. **What counts as a Mermaid fence.** An opening line matching §3's pattern, case-insensitively: `^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})[ \t]*mermaid(-example)?\b`. So `mermaid-example` is a Mermaid fence, and so is `Mermaid`. An unclosed fence runs to the end of the file. Fences inside other fenced blocks are skipped. 6. **Conflict markers (E).** A line starting `<<<<<<<`, `>>>>>>>` or `|||||||` followed by a space or end of line. A line that is exactly `=======` is not a marker on its own. In Markdown it underlines a setext heading, and the inputs may already hold one, so counting it would make a clean merge E. Git never writes `=======` without a `<<<<<<<` line before it, so a real conflict is still caught by that line. A marker anywhere in the merged file makes it E, for every stratum. §5.3 says this explicitly for stratum D, and its first sentence ("its merged file holds a conflict marker") reads as the whole file for all strata. 7. **`git ls-files -u` is not consulted.** The extractor sees only the four files, so an unmerged index entry with no marker in the file cannot be seen. 8. **Text normalisation.** UTF-8 (undecodable bytes are replaced), a leading BOM is dropped, and CRLF and CR become LF before parsing. ## "R does not parse" without R (§4.4) 9. **E versus OUT-OF-SUBSET when H fails on the merged diagram.** H sorts each failure into one of three kinds: - **noparse**: certain R failures, so the result is **E**. These are the ones §4.4 lists, and the Mermaid doc's own warning about `end`: - an unknown or mixed-case header (`UnknownDiagramError`); - `@{ shape: … }` with an uppercase letter or `_` ("No such shape"); - an out-of-range `linkStyle` index, counted against the edges defined *before* the statement; - more than 100,000 edges; - a `subgraph` without `end`, or `end` without a `subgraph`; - lowercase `end` used as a node id; - an unterminated front matter block. - **unsupported**: outside the subset, where R may well parse it. The result is **OUT-OF-SUBSET**. Any statement H cannot read lands here, because without R I cannot tell a broken text from a valid one H doesn't know. - **notflowchart**: see choice 11. 10. **An edge count over 100,000 is E, not OUT-OF-SUBSET.** With `maxEdges: 100000`, R throws "Edge limit exceeded", and §4.4 lists that among the texts that do not parse. For an input it simply means "not in the subset". 11. **G0 "no longer a flowchart".** If the header is a known non-flowchart Mermaid keyword (`sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `gantt`, …), the result is G0. A header that is no Mermaid diagram at all is E (choice 9). In Markdown mode, a merged file without exactly one Mermaid fence is G0. 12. **Order of outcomes.** 1. Conflict marker, then noparse: E. This applies even when an input is out of the subset. 2. Any input out of the subset: `INPUT-OUT-OF-SUBSET`, with no records. §5.3 says every other category needs four states in the subset. 3. G0. 4. Merged out of the subset: `OUT-OF-SUBSET` or `DUP-TITLE`. 5. Otherwise the records. ## The subset, as H reads it (Appendix A, §4.3) 13. **Ids.** ASCII letters, digits and `_`. A `-` is part of an id only when it isn't followed by `-`, `>` or `.`, and a `.` only when it isn't followed by `-` or `.`. This mirrors the docs' "dev--- ops" note. Non-ASCII ids are refused. Keywords used as ids (`subgraph`, `style`, `class`, `click`, `default`, …) are refused. 14. **Arrows.** Only the listed arrows and their longer forms: - `-->`, `---`, `--o`, `--x`, `<-->`, `o--o`, `x--x` - `-.->`, `-.-` - `==>`, `===` - `~~~` Anything else that R might accept is refused: `<==>`, `==o`, `x-->`, `<---`, a labelled `~~~`, and so on. A leading `o` or `x` head must follow whitespace, so it can't be read as part of the id. Kinds are normalised to `(line, start head, end head)` and length is dropped, as Appendix A says. 15. **Labels.** - Text is quoted (`"…"`) or unquoted. So `

Any other `<`, `>` or `&` is refused, because its sanitised form is not given. - Labels, titles and edge texts are trimmed, and one pair of surrounding quotes is stripped. - Multi-line labels and Markdown strings are refused. # CHOICES — extract2.py Each entry gives the rule and its section, what was ambiguous, and what `extract2.py` does. I wrote this from `SPEC.md` and `mermaid-12.1.0-flowchart.md` only. I could not run R (Mermaid 12.1.0) here. Where H has to agree with R on a behaviour that neither document states, the entry says **assumed R behaviour**. In those cases H refuses the text (out of the subset) unless I was confident about R. ## Invocation and output (Appendix D) 1. **Output shape.** One JSON object with these fields: - `outcome`: `decided`, `E`, `G0`, `OUT-OF-SUBSET`, `DUP-TITLE` or `INPUT-OUT-OF-SUBSET`. - `states`: H's verdict on each of the four files. - `decided`: every decided unit with its value, with `absent: true` for a decided absence. - `conflicts` and `undecided_memberships`. - `refusal_cases` (§5.2) and `exposure` (§5.5). - `new_lint_failures`. - `records`: each has `category`, `group`, `tier` and `objects`, plus detail about the unit. - `tiers`: a count of records per tier. The "—" tier is written `-`. 2. **Exit status.** A wrong argument count exits 2. Every verdict about the texts, including E and out-of-subset, exits 0 with JSON. An internal error exits non-zero with a traceback; it is not hidden. 3. **Order is not printed among the decided values.** The order class (§4.1) is decided pair by pair (choice 30) and is only reported as S-ORDER. ## Files, strata, fences (§5.3, Appendix C L6) 4. **Which strata are Markdown.** The spec names only stratum `D`. The diagram is read from a Mermaid fence when: - the base path ends in `.md`, `.markdown` or `.mdx`; or - the stratum is `D`; or - the base file contains a Mermaid fence. Otherwise the whole file is the diagram, and so is any `.mmd` or `.mermaid` file. 5. **What counts as a Mermaid fence.** An opening line matching §3's pattern, case-insensitively: `^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})[ \t]*mermaid(-example)?\b`. So `mermaid-example` is a Mermaid fence, and so is `Mermaid`. An unclosed fence runs to the end of the file. Fences inside other fenced blocks are skipped. 6. **Conflict markers (E).** A line starting `<<<<<<<`, `>>>>>>>` or `|||||||` followed by a space or end of line. A line that is exactly `=======` is not a marker on its own. In Markdown it underlines a setext heading, and the inputs may already hold one, so counting it would make a clean merge E. Git never writes `=======` without a `<<<<<<<` line before it, so a real conflict is still caught by that line. A marker anywhere in the merged file makes it E, for every stratum. §5.3 says this explicitly for stratum D, and its first sentence ("its merged file holds a conflict marker") reads as the whole file for all strata. 7. **`git ls-files -u` is not consulted.** The extractor sees only the four files, so an unmerged index entry with no marker in the file cannot be seen. 8. **Text normalisation.** UTF-8 (undecodable bytes are replaced), a leading BOM is dropped, and CRLF and CR become LF before parsing. ## "R does not parse" without R (§4.4) 9. **E versus OUT-OF-SUBSET when H fails on the merged diagram.** H sorts each failure into one of three kinds: - **noparse**: certain R failures, so the result is **E**. These are the ones §4.4 lists, and the Mermaid doc's own warning about `end`: - an unknown or mixed-case header (`UnknownDiagramError`); - `@{ shape: … }` with an uppercase letter or `_` ("No such shape"); - an out-of-range `linkStyle` index, counted against the edges defined *before* the statement; - more than 100,000 edges; - a `subgraph` without `end`, or `end` without a `subgraph`; - lowercase `end` used as a node id; - an unterminated front matter block. - **unsupported**: outside the subset, where R may well parse it. The result is **OUT-OF-SUBSET**.
